To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glucagon and insulin regulate hepatic BMAL1 expression through CREB/CRTC complex and CRTC2, respectively.

1) Glucagon-CreB/Crtc2 signaling axis plays a key role in regulating hepatic Bmal expression; 2) Glucagon activates CRTC2 by phosphorylation and CRTC2 is then recruited to the Bmal promoter; 3) Insulin suppresses fasting-induced Crtc2 activation and Bmal expression by inhibiting its activity after refeeding; 4) CRTC2 is also required for basal Bmal transcription
glucagon-CREB-CRTC2 signaling axis regulates the expression of Bmal1 through binding to the CREB site in the promoter region of Bmal1 gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of how the circadian clock regulates hepatic energy metabolism.
how the liver clock is synchronized to food availability.
the molecular basis of how glucagon/insuin metabolic cues regulate the hepatic clock and its implications on the circadian control of energy metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CRTC2 integrates glucagon and insulin signals to control hepatic BMAL1 expression, which is a key component of peripheral circadian oscillators.
glucagon/insulins regulate hepatic circadian gene expression through CRTC2.

the temporal signals, such as fasting and refeeding, are integrated into the hepatic circadian oscillator through the glucagon-CREB-CRTC2 signaling cascade, which is required for the transcription of Bma1.
